newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arbed more confident about 2nd half '97.
newsitem.headline: Arbed more confident about 2nd half '97.

text.p: Luxembourg steel maker Arbed SA said on Tuesday it was confident the steel market would pick up further in the second half of 1997, noting orders were up sharply compared with 1996.
"We are seeing a strengthening of European demand and a selective rise in (selling) prices," Arbed chief executive officer Joseph Kinsch told a news conference.
"We can be more confident for the second half of this year and if we believe the economists it should continue in 1998."

Asked whether the group would return to profit in 1997, he said only that from the second half, results would improve. Export markets were favourable due to the strength of the pound, the dollar and the Italian lira.

Kinsch said future objectives included finishing the integration off German unit Stahlwerke Bremen into the group and raising the plant's performance. The group also wanted to develop downstream activities and products of high added value.
Arbed would complete its transition to electric steel making with the startup of its new furnace at Belval where tests began this month. The last blast furnace will close in July or August.
Kinsch said that because of Luxembourg's location Arbed could negotiate competitive electricity contracts with Belgian, German and French supplyers.
Arbed would develop the strong position of its ALZ unit in flat stainless steel products. It expected stainless steel capacity to reach 700,000 tonnes by 1998 from 440,000 in 1996.
Arbed had group loss of 1.2 billion francs in 1996 after earning a net 3.7 billion in 1995.
